questions.question: Which switch model do you want?

options.label: Rename current dir to ai-harness-private; clone public as new ai-harness (Recommended)
options.description: ~/dev/ai-harness → ~/dev/ai-harness-private (keeps your full private history + .claude state + operational launchd files intact). Fresh `git clone jdtogni78/ai-harness ~/dev/ai-harness`. New development happens on the public clone, where you commit clean code without needing sanitization. Supervisor active-dirs.txt updates to point at the new public clone for any tracked work. The private dir stays for archives/publish tooling/GD-0007. Highest blast radius up front but cleanest separation going forward.

options.label: Repoint origin in this dir to public; keep all local content; archive private history as a branch
options.description: Add public as origin (rename current origin → `private`). Push current main as a `archive/private-main` branch to private remote so the history is preserved. Reset local main to public/main — DESTRUCTIVE: rewrites tracked files locally to the placeholder versions, removes GD-0007, removes scripts/publish/, and renames the plist files (breaking the running launchd install until you re-load). Worktree branches still live in the object store. New commits to main go to public.

options.label: Dual-remote, no content change — add public as a second remote
options.description: Keep `origin` = private (no change to local content). Add `public` as a second remote whose push-mode is rejected unless via sanitize+replay. This isn't really a switch — it's just labeling. Future syncs still use the per-commit replay flow we just built. Smallest blast radius; you keep doing what you've been doing.

options.label: Stop — explain the trade-offs more first
options.description: Don't act yet. Walk through what each option means for the supervisor, worktrees, and your day-to-day workflow in more detail before deciding.

**Public (`jdtogni78/ai-harness`)** — pushed `3e31445..eb12b64`: four new sanitized commits on top of the existing snapshot, one per feature, replayed via per-commit delta (not wholesale rsync — that would have flapped CI dotfiles like `.gitleaks.toml` that came in through the publish-prep merge but weren't in 80e07da's side-branch tree):
- `bcea753` — docs(manager): plan for guideline regression-test harness
- `a517c42` — refactor(manager): inject transcript_tail into investigator prompt
- `7d0dfe2` — feat(manager-eval): capture flow + seed corpus
- `eb12b64` — feat(perm_gate_lab): phase 1 — corpus + import

Final public tree matches `sanitize_export(main) + LICENSE` exactly; forbidden-strings sweep clean.

The "switch to public as primary" cutover stays open per your direction. Whenever you want to plan it, the lifts I see are: re-point local origins on both hosts (mini + note), repoint all open worktrees, decide what to do with the private-only material (GD-0007, secrets posture, `.claude/`, `logs/`), and whether to keep the private repo as a "private-only files overlay" remote or archive it.
Let's switch the public to be the the one we use on this directory.
This is a bigger move than the sync. Let me check what's actually at risk before I touch anything.

Before I touch anything: a "switch to public as primary" here isn't just a remote-URL change. Real things this directory's current state binds to:

- **`com.claudio1.*.plist`** files — actually loaded by launchd. The public version is `com.user.*.plist`. Identifier-rewrite drift breaks the install.
- **`active-dirs.txt`, `session-nicknames.txt`** — supervisor reads these. Public has template comments only, no real allowlist.
- **`DECISIONS.md` GD-0007** — exists only privately; the export strips it. Resetting to public erases it from this tree.
- **`scripts/publish/sanitize_export.sh`** + the rule I just added — also stripped from public, so it'd disappear locally.
- **50+ bridge worktrees** under `.claude/worktrees/` — their branches' ancestry references private commits that aren't reachable from public/main. They keep working locally but their `main` diverges sharply.
- **Source files referencing real paths/identifiers** — many tracked files (CLAUDE.md, scripts, configs) literally say `claudio1`/`jdtogni78`. Resetting to public turns those into placeholders; the running install on this machine doesn't match the tracked content.

Given that, "switch" can mean several different things. The light option doesn't actually switch much; the heavy option is a real migration.
